title: Orbit's newsletter kit
brief:
Orbit's newsletter, The Orbit Dispatch, is written each month by people and agents who aren't designers. Build the reusable part of it: what every issue is made with, so that an issue can't go off Orbit's brand.

An issue gives three things: its preview text, its heading, and its body (an intro, then stories: each an image, a title, a sentence and a button).

What every issue must keep, whatever its body:

- Orbit's header, the logo (https://assets.orbit.dev/img/orbit-logo.png, 252×128, shown 126px wide, alt "Orbit"), at the top, the same in every issue.
- Orbit's footer, the same in every issue: "Orbit Labs, 500 Market St, San Francisco" and an "Unsubscribe" link to https://orbit.dev/unsubscribe?utm_source=newsletter.
- A white 600px card on a #f1f2f6 page.
- Colors only from Orbit's palette: page #f1f2f6, card #ffffff, text #1f2937, muted #6b7280, accent #4f46e5 (buttons), and #ffffff on the accent. Nothing in a body may change them.
- Text in Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif. Nothing in a body may change it.
- Every link on orbit.dev or a subdomain, with ?utm_source=newsletter.
- Alt text on every image, a preview text, and at least one button in the body.
- No markup a body brings of its own.

Make the newsletter refuse a body that would break one of these where your tool can; where it can't, write the rule down for whoever writes an issue.

spec.preview: What's new at Orbit this month, in two minutes.
texts: Two things from the Orbit team this month.
Typing, search and preview are all twice as fast.
Orbit Labs, 500 Market St, San Francisco

run.prompt: Build Orbit's reusable newsletter as BRIEF.md describes, following CLAUDE.md. It's done when `node tools/check.mjs` passes.
